Clear signage on a typical week
This section sets out what is expected

Companion Animal Travel Desk Standards

This section supports careful, calm handling of animals and documents so each journey is arranged with steady attention and clear handoffs. The desk must treat the traveler, the welfare coordinator, and the ground team as part of one shared process, with comfort and safety given equal weight throughout.

Staff must confirm the animal type, carrier details, and travel notes before acceptance, and they must speak plainly when a request does not meet our conditions. Any crate or carrier brought to the desk must be clean, secure, and easy to inspect, with enough room for the animal to stand, turn, and rest without strain. <<FACT F068>> If a carrier looks unsafe, cramped, damaged, or poorly ventilated, the agent must pause the check-in and seek a review from the senior coordinator. For reptile transport, staff must follow the applicable fee guidance exactly. <<FACT F060>> The fee outcome is handled without debate at the counter, and staff should keep the discussion brief, respectful, and focused on the booking record.

The desk must check that the traveler has brought the required papers, that labels are clear, and that care notes are visible to the team that will handle the animal next. When there is any sign of distress, overheating, injury, or agitation, the matter must be escalated at once and the animal must not be moved forward until the concern is resolved. Mei Bianchi, Ines Khan, and any other traveler should receive the same steady explanation of next steps, because reassurance lowers confusion and reduces delay. Pip or any other pet must never be left unattended in the public area, even for a short handoff.

Records must be complete, readable, and entered in the same shift whenever possible, with any exception passed on clearly to the next coordinator. The desk should keep movement gentle, avoid unnecessary noise, and give extra care during busy periods so the animal is not rushed.

If anything remains unclear, contact the senior coordinator or the duty manager at once.
